purpose: Bounded names/presence and API-key policy lookup for an existing configured Core admin service credential.
policy_interpretation: Persisted API keys are enabled and endpoint restrictions disabled. The empty allowed-endpoints list is therefore not a restriction under this policy. No relevant configured override was present in the known JSON inputs or Main unit/drop-ins; process environment and the in-memory Config object were not inspected.
bounded_absence: No named Core/admin/deployment service API-key credential reference was found in the known runtime-environment JSON, resolver JSON, Main unit or its two actual declared drop-ins. Those units declare no EnvironmentFile or credential source. This does not assert that no unused user API key exists elsewhere; user/API-key rows and unreferenced secret stores were not searched.
exact_missing_item: An already provisioned Core admin service API-key credential, bound to an existing admin identity and available through an authorized deployment reference, has not been established. A current authenticated administrator session is the other supported source of the required task proof.
next_safe_action: Root can use an existing authorized admin session or a verified already provisioned admin service credential through normal authentication to obtain genuine current /api/tasks evidence. Do not mint an owner/user token, create a key, promote a user, relax endpoint restrictions, reuse old task proof or treat DB counts as task quiescence.
